items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: And the band that I joined was the band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson, Wynton Kelly, Melba Liston was the musical director

ctx.x: Well I think you had a good positive effect on what he was able to do. Would you agree with that?

Well I’ll tell you, we have to look at that. Because I joined Dizzy’s band in either the late fifties or the early sixties. And the band that I joined was the band with Lee Morgan, Benny Golson, Wynton Kelly, Melba Liston was the musical director, and they were playing so much music man, my head was just — they had my head spinning. I never wrote anything for the band. Because the music that they were playing, the arrangements were so good that I just didn’t feel like I wanted to try to write something coming up…
Yeah. Is there certain things that he liked to hear? Is it possible to answer that? I mean certain tempos, feels? I know he loved Latin grooves.

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was Melba, and Chuck Connors, who played with Duke’s band, and another trombone player.

ctx.x: Yeah. He paid a good price for the music. He paid the guys good. Some guys were making more than me, because they were doing things – more important things in the band than I was.
Who was in the trombone section with you?

It was Melba, and Chuck Connors, who played with Duke’s band, and another trombone player. I think his name was Willie. Something like that. Was from – I forget where he was from. They were good players. They were very good.

items.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One you had Slide Hampton, Frank Rehak.

ctx.x: No. I had them all changed about now.

But you had two separate ’bone sections on two different record dates. One was around Christmas time – they both were around Christmas time – one around the 22nd, one around the 24th. One you had Slide Hampton, Frank Rehak.
Oh. That was a different Company altogether. I forgot about that. And Randy, we had a date with him and the 4 ’bones too. I’ll play it for you when we get finished with this.
